title: org-lsp configuration
description: The options of the org-lsp server, in its shared configuration file. See docs/configuration.md.

org_agenda_files.description: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

org_todo_keywords.description: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

org_log_done.description: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. A file's `#+STARTUP:` words `logdone`, `lognotedone` and `nologdone` change it there; an entry's `LOGGING` property (inherited) says what its state changes log instead: those words, `logrepeat` and its relatives, and keywords with what they log (`WAIT(@/!)`), or `nil` for nothing. (`org-log-done`)

org_log_repeat.description: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. `#+STARTUP:` `logrepeat`, `lognoterepeat` and `nologrepeat` change it in a file, and the `LOGGING` property in an entry. (`org-log-repeat`)

org_log_into_drawer.description: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. `#+STARTUP:` `logdrawer` and `nologdrawer` change it in a file; an entry's `LOG_INTO_DRAWER` property (inherited) says which drawer for it (`t` for `LOGBOOK`, `nil` for none). (`org-log-into-drawer`)

org_tags_column.description: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

org_use_tag_inheritance.description: Which tags entries inherit from their parents and from `#+FILETAGS:`: `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of tags, or a regexp (Emacs syntax) tags must match. Inherited tags count in tag searches and show in the agenda. (`org-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_tags_exclude_from_inheritance.description: Tags never inherited, when `org_use_tag_inheritance` is `true` or a regexp. (`org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance`)

org_use_property_inheritance.description: Which properties an entry without them takes from its parents, the file's property drawer and `#+PROPERTY:` lines, in property searches (`OWNER="alice"`): `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of names, or a regexp (Emacs syntax). `CATEGORY` and `ARCHIVE` are always inherited. (`org-use-property-inheritance`)

org_global_properties.description: Properties every entry inherits, after those of `#+PROPERTY:` lines: chiefly the allowed values of a property, which setting it offers and `S-<right>` and `S-<left>` go through on its line (`{ "Effort_ALL": "0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00" }`; `:ETC` allows others too). (`org-global-properties`)

org_clock_into_drawer.description: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `org_log_into_drawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

org_clock_out_remove_zero_time_clocks.description: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

org_clock_out_when_done.description: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

org_clock_in_switch_to_state.description: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock starts on it (`NEXT`), unless it has it already. (`org-clock-in-switch-to-state`)

org_clock_out_switch_to_state.description: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock stops on it. (`org-clock-out-switch-to-state`)

org_complete_tags_always_offer_all_agend.description: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. Setting tags offers them too. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

org_cite_global_bibliography.description: Bibliography files for the citations of every document (`[cite:@key]`), after those its `#+BIBLIOGRAPHY:` lines name: BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`) or CSL-JSON (`.json`). Their entries are completed after `@`, shown over a key, and where following a key goes; a key none has is marked. (`org-cite-global-bibliography`)

org_tag_alist.description: The tags offered when setting tags in a file without a `#+TAGS:` line, written like one: `"work(w) home(h) { @office(o) @home(m) } [ GTD : Control Persp ]"` gives `work` the key `w`, makes `@office` and `@home` exclusive, and groups `Control` and `Persp` under `GTD`; `\n` starts a new line. A list of these words does as well. Unset, the tags used in the file are offered. (`org-tag-alist`)

org_tag_persistent_alist.description: Tags offered in every file, before those of `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`, written the same way. (`org-tag-persistent-alist`)

org_group_tags.description: A group tag (`[ GTD : Control Persp ]`, `{ Context : @home @office }` in `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`) in the match string of a tags view stands for itself and the tags of its group. (`org-group-tags`)

org_use_fast_tag_selection.description: Pick tags by key, each key turning its tag on or off until RET: `auto` when some tag has a key, `true` always (keys are given to the tags without one), `false` never: the tags are typed instead. (`org-use-fast-tag-selection`)

org_fast_tag_selection_single_key.description: In fast tag selection, the first key that changes the tags also ends it. (`org-fast-tag-selection-single-key`)

org_tags_sort_function.description: Sort the tags of a headline when they are set: alphabetically, or the other way. (`org-tags-sort-function`)

org_auto_align_tags.description: Align the tags of a headline to `org_tags_column` when they are set. (`org-auto-align-tags`)

org_todo_repeat_to_state.description: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

org_priority_default.description: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

org_priority_start_cycle_with_default.description: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

org_time_stamp_rounding_minutes.description: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

org_read_date_prefer_future.description: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

org_read_date_force_compatible_dates.description: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

org_refile_targets.description: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxlevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

org_refile_use_outline_path.description: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

org_reverse_note_order.description: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

org_archive_location.description: Where archived subtrees go: a file, `::`, and a headline under which they go (they go to the end of the file without one). `%s` is the name of the file the subtree is in; an empty file part is that file. `datetree/` as the headline files them under year, month and day, by when they were closed. An `ARCHIVE` property of the entry or a parent, or a `#+ARCHIVE:` line, says otherwise. (`org-archive-location`)

org_archive_reversed_order.description: An archived subtree goes first under its archive headline, not last. (`org-archive-reversed-order`)

org_archive_mark_done.description: Mark archived entries done: `true` for the first done keyword, or the keyword to use. (`org-archive-mark-done`)

org_archive_subtree_add_inherited_tags.description: Give an archived subtree the tags it inherited: always, never, or when it stays in its file. (`org-archive-subtree-add-inherited-tags`)

org_archive_save_context_info.description: What an archived entry keeps as `ARCHIVE_…` properties: `time`, `file`, `olpath` (its outline path), `category`, `todo`, `itags` (inherited tags), `ltags` (its own tags) and `olid` (its parent's ID). (`org-archive-save-context-info`)

org_archive_sibling_heading.description: The headline of the sibling `org.archive.sibling` archives under. (`org-archive-sibling-heading`)

org_archive_file_header_format.description: What a new archive file starts with; `%s` is the path of the file the subtree came from. (`org-archive-file-header-format`)

org_archive_default_command.description: What `org.archive.default` does: archive the subtree, archive it under its sibling, or tag it. (`org-archive-default-command`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path

type.description: An Org entry (the default), or plain text

org_capture_templates.description: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, or `plain`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `empty_lines`, `empty_lines_before`, `empty_lines_after` and `immediate_finish`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path. An empty path is `org_default_notes_file`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `org_default_notes_file`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

org_directory.description: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

org_default_notes_file.description: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

org_link_descriptive.description: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

org_hide_emphasis_markers.description: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

return_uses_meta_return.description: RET on the first line of a list item makes the next item, numbered and with a checkbox as M-RET (`org-meta-return`) makes it, the items after it renumbered, as nvim-orgmode's `org_return_uses_meta_return` does. Off, RET is Org's: a new line in the item. `org.return.item` (`<S-CR>`, Shift+Enter, with the vim keys) always does it.

auto_save.description: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.

org_cycle_separator_lines.description: With at least this many blank lines after a subtree, the last one stays outside its fold. Negative: all of them stay outside. `0`: none does. (`org-cycle-separator-lines`)

org_adapt_indentation.description: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

org_startup_indented.description: Show files indented by level without changing them (`org-indent-mode`): the text under a headline lines up with its title, and leading stars are hidden. `#+STARTUP: indent` and `noindent` decide for a file. It turns `org_adapt_indentation` off in such files, unless that is `"headline-data"`. Editors that can show it: Neovim, and VS Code (not on wrapped lines). (`org-startup-indented`)

org_hide_leading_stars.description: Hide all the stars of a headline but the last; they keep their place. `#+STARTUP: hidestars` and `showstars` decide for a file. (`org-hide-leading-stars`)

org_src_preserve_indentation.description: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

org_edit_src_content_indentation.description: How far code is indented past its source block when re-indenting. (`org-edit-src-content-indentation`)

org_agenda_span.description: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

org_agenda_start_on_weekday.description: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

org_deadline_warning_days.description: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

org_scheduled_delay_days.description: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

org_scheduled_past_days.description: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

org_deadline_past_days.description: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_done.description: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_if_done.description: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_timestamp_if_done.description: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

org_agenda_show_future_repeats.description: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

org_agenda_tags_column.description: Where tags are aligned in the agenda: a column (negative: where they end), or `auto` for the right edge of the window. With `auto`, the editors that tell the server how wide the agenda's window is (Neovim, Vim, Sublime Text) have the tags there, and the agenda follows the window as it is resized; the others (VS Code, Zed) have them end at column 80. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

org_agenda_time_grid.description: The time grid, as Org writes it: the days that have it (`daily`: a one-day agenda; `weekly`: every day of a longer one; `today`: today; `require-timed`: only days with an entry that has a time; `remove-match`: no grid line at a time an entry already has), the times of its lines (`800` for 8:00), what follows a time that has no end time, and the text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

org_agenda_current_time_string.description: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

org_agenda_show_current_time_in_grid.description: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

org_agenda_weekend_days.description: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

org_agenda_start_with_log_mode.description: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_clockreport_mode.description: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_archives_mode.description: Start the agenda with entries in archived trees (`trees`; `v a` toggles it), or those and the files the agenda files archive to (`files`; `v A`). (`org-agenda-start-with-archives-mode`)

org_agenda_log_mode_items.description: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

org_agenda_persistent_marks.description: Keep the marks of a bulk action (`B`) after it (`p` in its menu toggles this for one action). (`org-agenda-persistent-marks`)

org_agenda_start_with_follow_mode.description: Start the agenda in follow mode, which shows the entry of the cursor's line in another window as the cursor moves (`F` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-follow-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_entry_text_mode.description: Start the agenda with some text of each entry under its line (`E` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-entry-text-mode`)

org_agenda_entry_text_maxlines.description: The most lines of an entry's text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-maxlines`)

org_agenda_entry_text_leaders.description: What each line of an entry's text starts with in the agenda. (`org-agenda-entry-text-leaders`)

org_agenda_entry_text_exclude_regexps.description: Emacs regexps whose matches are left out of the entry text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-exclude-regexps`)

org_agenda_block_separator.description: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

org_agenda_compact_blocks.description: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

agenda_hide_empty_blocks.description: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

org_agenda_search_view_always_boolean.description: Read every search string of the search view (`s`) as words that must (`+word`, `word`) or must not (`-word`) occur, `{regexp}`s and `"quoted phrases"`. Off, it is a phrase whose spaces match any whitespace, unless its first word starts with `+`, `-` or `{`. (`org-agenda-search-view-always-boolean`)

org_agenda_search_view_force_full_words.description: The words of a Boolean search match whole words only, as a search string starting with `:` asks. (`org-agenda-search-view-force-full-words`)

org_agenda_search_view_max_outline_level.description: The search view shows headlines down to this level, a match below one counting for the headline above: 0 for every level. (`org-agenda-search-view-max-outline-level`)

org_agenda_text_search_extra_files.description: Files the search view (`s`) searches besides the agenda files, after them, as `org_agenda_files` names them. `agenda-archives` first adds the files the agenda files archive to. A file listed twice is searched at its last place. (`org-agenda-text-search-extra-files`)

org_agenda_prefix_format.description: What comes before the headline on a line of the agenda (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), tags searches (`tags`) and text searches (`search`): `%c` the category, `%t` the time, `%s` the leader (`Scheduled: `), `%e` the effort, `%l` a blank per level, `%T` the last tag, `%b` the headlines above (breadcrumbs), `%i` the icon (none). A width pads (`%-12c` on the right, `%12c` on the left), `.N` cuts, `%?` leaves out an empty field, and a character before the letter follows a value that is not empty (`%-12:c`). `%(…)` (Emacs Lisp) is left empty. (`org-agenda-prefix-format`)

org_agenda_todo_keyword_format.description: How a TODO keyword is written in the agenda: `%-4s` pads it to four columns, so that the titles line up; an empty format leaves keywords out. (`org-agenda-todo-keyword-format`)

org_agenda_scheduled_leaders.description: The leader of a scheduled entry on its day, and on today when its day has passed (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-scheduled-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_leaders.description: The leader of a deadline on its day, on today before it (`%d`: the days left), and on today after it (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-deadline-leaders`)

org_agenda_timerange_leaders.description: The leader of a time range within a day, and of a range over days (`%d`: which day of it, `%d`: how many days). (`org-agenda-timerange-leaders`)

org_agenda_remove_tags.description: Leave the tags out of the agenda's lines; `prefix` only when the prefix shows a tag (`%T`). (`org-agenda-remove-tags`)

org_stuck_projects.description: What the stuck projects view (`#`) lists: the projects the match string finds whose subtree has no entry with one of the TODO keywords (`*` for any not done) or tags (`*` for any), and no match of the regexp. (`org-stuck-projects`)

org_agenda_breadcrumbs_separator.description: What goes between the headlines of `%b`. (`org-agenda-breadcrumbs-separator`)

org_agenda_format_date.description: How the agenda writes a day, as `format-time-string` does: `%A %d %B %Y`, `%a %Y-%m-%d`. (`org-agenda-format-date`)

org_agenda_start_day.description: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

key.description: The keys that pick the command in the agenda menu

match.description: For todo, keywords (NEXT|WAIT); for tags, a match string (work-home, PRIORITY="A")

settings.description: Agenda options for this command: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

org_agenda_custom_commands.description: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`org_agenda_span`, `org_agenda_start_day`…). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
